alert_rule: Calibrated Safety Margin: Alert if Model + 6 µg/m³ >= 60 µg/m³ (97.5% Decision Accuracy, 96.9% Recall, 2 False Alarms)

pre_season_before_oct_15.description: Low-pollution summer/monsoon days. High atmospheric mixing and precipitation washout.

smog_season_from_oct_15.description: High-pollution autumn/winter days. Shallow boundary layer inversions, crop stubble smoke, and Diwali firecrackers.

interval_diagnostics.explanation: Because a Gradient Boosting Machine fits non-linear patterns closely, in-sample training residuals are artificially compact. In the test set, while pre-season coverage is 97.8%, coverage collapses to 34.5% during peak winter smog because fixed ±20.5 µg/m³ bounds are too narrow for extreme 100–300 µg/m³ winter atmospheric swings.

worst_failures.hypothesis: Hypothesis: Episodic Firecracker Detonation + Severe Inversion. Unmetered festive firecracker emissions released a massive localized particulate burst. Concurrently, nocturnal winds dropped below 1.2 m/s, compressing smoke into the lowest 100m. Non-linear tree regressors cannot extrapolate beyond historical quantile limits for unmeasured human festive bursts.
worst_failures.operational_impact: Crucial Safety Win: Although point forecast was 216.5 µg/m³ (under-predicting 317.0 µg/m³), both 216.5 µg/m³ and the upper bound (237.0 µg/m³) were far above 60 µg/m³. An unequivocal Crimson Alert was issued, cancelling outdoor morning assembly and protecting students.

worst_failures.category: Severe Under-Forecast (Upwind Stubble Incursion & Lag Shadow)
worst_failures.hypothesis: Hypothesis: Stubble Burning Transport & Lag Shadow. An intense agricultural crop burning plume from Punjab/Haryana was advected overnight into Delhi. Because the preceding day (31 Oct) had clean air (90.6 µg/m³), the heavily weighted lag_1 and rolling 3d features anchored the tree prediction too low, creating a 24-hr lag shadow.
worst_failures.operational_impact: Safety Win: Predicted 90.2 µg/m³ > 60 µg/m³ threshold. The system correctly issued an Amber Alert, relocating morning assembly indoors.

worst_failures.hypothesis: Hypothesis: Stagnation Feedback Loop. Three consecutive calm days allowed boundary layer pollution to compound faster than standard linear advection estimates anticipate.
worst_failures.operational_impact: Safety Win: Predicted 160.8 µg/m³ exceeded 60 µg/m³. Crimson alert active, all outdoor athletic training suspended.

worst_failures.hypothesis: Hypothesis: Secondary Aerosol Formation. High relative humidity combined with nocturnal cold temperatures accelerated gas-to-particle conversion (sulfates and nitrates) in the troposphere.
worst_failures.operational_impact: Safety Win: Predicted 214.8 µg/m³ triggered full emergency indoor protocols.

worst_failures.hypothesis: Hypothesis: Boundary Layer Compression. Rapid onset of winter nocturnal cooling trapped surface vehicular and industrial emissions overnight.
worst_failures.operational_impact: Safety Win: Predicted 193.3 µg/m³ triggered full indoor PE directives.

flagship_case_study.why_it_failed: Episodic human firecracker combustion and calm surface winds (<1.2 m/s) created an unmeasured, non-linear particulate spike that gradient boosting trees cannot extrapolate from weather alone.
flagship_case_study.why_the_decision_engine_succeeded: Even though point forecast underestimated the 317 µg/m³ peak by 100 µg/m³, predicted 216.5 µg/m³ far exceeded the 60 µg/m³ safety threshold! The school gate issued an unequivocal Crimson Alert, cancelling outdoor assembly and saving 2,400 students from toxic exposure.

data_quality.methodological_limitation: Missing OpenAQ days were dropped prior to building row-based lag features, causing features following the 14-day late-September gap to reference non-consecutive calendar days.

diwali_experiment_metadata.scientific_conclusion: Log-ratio target formulation improves seasonal and overall RMSE, but calendar features produce negligible Diwali window MAE reduction due to sample scarcity (1 test event) and unmetered human combustion.
